prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's density relaxation is gated only on global overflow and worst-region density, but the TNS/WNS cost comes from *timing-critical* cells being pushed into dense regions; make the early quadratic ramp of the density weight start later (longer window) and additionally keep a slightly higher floor on `mu` when HPWL is improving, so the placer spends more iterations in the wirelength-friendly regime where critical nets stay short, reducing TNS.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.509 robust(mean-std)=+0.149 min_case=+0.141 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.141 dWNS=+2.7% dTNS=+21.5% overflow~110
  bp-ng45: score=+0.186 dWNS=+17.4% dTNS=+19.3% overflow~145
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.182 dWNS=+2.3% dTNS=+28.4% overflow~114
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with TNS gains (+19–28%) exceeding WNS gains, consistent with keeping critical nets short during the wirelength-friendly regime. bp-ng45 showed the largest WNS move (+17.4%), suggesting the delayed density ramp most helped its timing-critical cells. Overflow stayed ~110–145, so no legality cost. Next step: sweep the ramp-start offset and `mu` floor jointly on bp-ng45 to find whether the WNS gain saturates before overflow degrades, confirming the mechanism rather than a single lucky setting.
